text.en: Asha read about a bomb that changed the world in 1945. "How did the war begin?" she asked.

World War II (1939-1945) began when Germany invaded Poland. It was fought between the Allies (Britain, France, the USSR, the USA) and the Axis (Germany, Italy, Japan). Germany swept through Europe with a fast attack called blitzkrieg.
The war spread when Germany attacked the USSR in 1941 and Japan attacked Pearl Harbor, bringing in the USA. The tide turned at Stalingrad and in the D-Day landings of 1944. Germany surrendered in May 1945.
The USA dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945, and Japan surrendered. Millions were killed, including the Jews in the Holocaust. The cost made the world seek lasting peace.

On 1 September 1939, German tanks and dive-bombers invaded Poland in a lightning blitzkrieg attack; two days later Britain and France declared war.

board.text: 1 Sep 1939: Invasion of Poland begins WWII

text.en: In spring 1940, Germany swept across Denmark, Norway, Belgium and France, forcing British forces into a dramatic rescue across the sea from Dunkirk.
Britain stood alone in the Battle of Britain, where Royal Air Force pilots and new radar technology thwarted Hitler's air offensive.

board.text: Battle of Britain: RAF & radar hold out

text.en: In June 1941, Hitler tore up his pact with Stalin and launched Operation Barbarossa, invading the Soviet Union along a massive Eastern Front.
On 7 December 1941, Japan bombed the US naval base at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii, pulling the industrial might of the United States into the war.

board.text: 7 Dec 1941: Pearl Harbor brings in USA

text.en: Japan quickly overran Southeast Asia, Malaya and Burma right up to India's eastern borders, sparking battles at Imphal and Kohima where Indian troops fought bravely.

board.text: Japan advances to Burma, Imphal & Kohima

text.en: Back at home in 1942, Indian nationalists launched Quit India, while Subhas Chandra Bose led the Azad Hind Fauj (INA) hoping to win independence.

board.text: India during WWII: Quit India & INA

text.en: Three decisive Allied turning points arrived in 1942–43: Midway in the Pacific, El Alamein in North Africa, and Stalingrad in snowy Russia.
At Stalingrad, fierce Soviet defence encircled the German Sixth Army—a shattering defeat from which Germany never recovered.

board.text: Stalingrad halts Nazi advance in the East

text.en: Under Nazi rule, conquered Europe suffered the Holocaust—the systematic industrial genocide that murdered six million Jews alongside millions of others.
On 6 June 1944—D-Day—Allied troops landed on Normandy beaches in France under General Eisenhower to open a Western Front and liberate Paris.
Meanwhile Allied science accelerated radar, penicillin antibiotics, jet engines, long-range rockets and secret codebreaking at Bletchley Park.
Squeezed from East and West, Soviet and American troops met at the Elbe; Hitler died in his Berlin bunker, and Germany surrendered on 8 May 1945 (VE Day).
In the Pacific, US forces island-hopped closer to Japan through fierce battles like Iwo Jima and Okinawa while Allied leaders met at Potsdam.
To force rapid surrender without invading Japan, the USA dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima (6 August) and Nagasaki (9 August 1945).
Japan surrendered formally on 2 September 1945 (VJ Day), ending the deadliest conflict in human history with over 60 million lives lost.
After the war, the Nuremberg and Tokyo trials held Nazi and militarist leaders legally accountable for war crimes and crimes against humanity.
To replace the failed League of Nations, fifty countries signed the United Nations Charter at San Francisco in 1945 to safeguard peace and human rights.

board.text: 1945: United Nations founded for world peace

text.en: Economic institutions—the World Bank and IMF from Bretton Woods—were built alongside UN agencies like UNESCO, WHO and UNICEF.

board.text: Bretton Woods: IMF, World Bank & UNICEF

text.en: Exhausted European empires could no longer hold vast colonies, clearing the way for Indian Independence in 1947 and Asian-African freedom.
Follow the arc: Blitzkrieg & Pearl Harbor -> Stalingrad & D-Day -> Atomic end -> UN & independence movements.

board.text: Axis surge -> Allied turn -> UN & Freedom

text.en: World War II taught humanity the horror of hatred and nuclear weapons—making human rights and peaceful cooperation our shared duty.

board.text: Human rights & peace over nuclear war

problem.en: Why are Stalingrad, El Alamein and Midway called the three major turning points of World War II?

text.en: Before late 1942: Axis momentum.

why.en: Germany held most of Europe and pushed deep into Russia and Egypt, while Japan dominated the Western Pacific.

text.en: Trace the three Allied reversals.

why.en: British forces halted Germany at El Alamein, Soviet armies trapped Germany at Stalingrad, and US carriers sank Japan's main fleet at Midway.

text.en: See what changed afterward.

why.en: From 1943 onward, the Axis powers were pushed onto the defensive on every front until final surrender in 1945.

prompt.en: A friend says Japan was an Allied power. How will you reply?

points.en: Pearl Harbor brought in the USA.
